newsitem.title: UK: Johnson Matthey bounces on relief at data.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Matthey bounces on relief at data.

text.p: Shares in Johnson Matthey were marked higher on Thursday in pre-market dealings after the metals and industrial materials group announced first-half profits rose nine percent.

Johnson Matthey shares, which have slid this year from a high of 669p, were indicated 8-1/2p higher at 542-1/2p in early trade. The stock, with 132,400 shares traded, counted among London's 10 most-active shares.
"This is a bounce on relief. There was a lot of talk about a horror scenario and that has weighed on the shares. But these are by no means a stunning set of figures," one dealer said.
"This is classic dead-cat stuff...The shares have come off so far this year and people had built up some pretty horrendous expectations," a second marketmaker said.
He said the figures were generally uninspiring and noted that the company said trading conditions remained difficult in some markets.
"The ceramics business doesn't look too positive," he said.
Johnson Matthey said Cookson Matthey Ceramics had a disappointing first half, with growth held back by depressed European tile markets.
